title: Integral stratified lfp constructibility agrees with finite constant local models
statement:
Let $\ell$ be a prime, $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ a finite extension, $A=\mathcal O_E$ its valuation ring [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension], and $X$ a Noetherian scheme, meaning quasi-compact [def-weil-pbc-quasi-compact-scheme] and locally Noetherian [pqf-def-locnoeth]. Give $A$ its valuation topology and put $B_X=p_X^*\underline A$ [sk-def-sfb-condensed-ring, sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients] on the small pro-étale site [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]. Let $M$ be a sheaf of $B_X$-modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. The following conditions are equivalent:

(i) $M$ is constructible in the general ring-object sense [def-sfb-constructible-module]: it admits a finite constructible locally closed stratification [def-constructible-stratification] on every stratum $T$ of which its restriction is locally finitely presented over $B_T$ [def-sfb-locally-finitely-presented]. Thus on a pro-étale covering of $T$ it is the cokernel of a morphism $B_V^m\to B_V^n$ for finite nonnegative integers $m,n$; the matrix entries are arbitrary sections of $B_V$.

(ii) $M$ is constructible in the finite constant local model sense [sk-def-sfb-constructible]: it admits a finite constructible locally closed stratification on every stratum $T$ of which there is a pro-étale covering $\{V_j\to T\}$ and finitely presented scalar $A$-modules $P_j$ [def-sc-finitely-presented-module] with
$$M|_{V_j}\cong B_{V_j}\otimes_A P_j.$$
Here $A$ and $P_j$ denote constant sheaves, and the tensor is extension along the constant-section map $A\to B_{V_j}$. Finitely presented means that $P_j$ is a cokernel of a scalar matrix $A^{u_j}\to A^{v_j}$ of finite size. The stratifications in (i) and (ii) may differ. Torsion scalar modules are allowed. No completeness, finite-dimension, separatedness, finite-type or invertibility assumption is imposed beyond the stated Noetherian hypothesis on $X$.

source.place: Hemo–Richarz–Scholbach Example 3.1 (continuous-function coefficient rings), Theorem 4.13 (pro-étale-local perfect-constant characterization), Theorem 6.2(2) (the lisse heart consists of finitely presented scalar local models), Theorem 6.2(3) (the constructible heart), Lemma 6.10 and Corollary 6.11(1) (t-admissibility for the valuation ring), and Theorem 6.12(2) (regular coherence of continuous-function rings). Compare Bhatt–Scholze Definition 6.8.10 and Proposition 6.8.11(3). The local-finite-presentation-to-perfect step is part of this coefficient-specific comparison obligation, not a verbatim consequence of the cited heart characterization.

proof.text: Use the same finite constructible stratification from general constructibility. Its immersions embed their Noetherian underlying spaces in X. Normalize each stratum coefficient ring by the canonical pullback isomorphism; local finite presentation is invariant under this ring isomorphism.

On a finite-presentation pro-etale cover choose the actual presentation morphisms. The spectral absolute value is nonarchimedean, hence the lattice integer subring is totally disconnected and Hausdorff. Use the canonical universe-polymorphic continuous realization to form each full scalar cokernel class. These agree at comparable points by continuity and Hausdorffness, and agree over equal base points by compatible geometric evaluation.

The covering maps are flat and jointly surjective. Apply arbitrary-type specialization-invariant flat descent on the Noetherian stratum. Pulling its locally constant class function back to each covering member makes that presentation fibre-type function locally constant.

Apply the single-presentation constant-type cokernel theorem to each covering member. Transport the result through the chosen presentation isomorphism. Bind the covering and its local-model coverings; the canonical module pullback composition isomorphism identifies the resulting models. Retain the original stratification.

Conversely each finite constant local model is locally finitely presented. On each stratum transport this local finite presentation back across the canonical coefficient isomorphism, using extension-of-scalars equals restriction along its inverse. The same stratification proves general constructibility. Since X is qcqs, the finite-constant-model predicate is exactly the stratified one.

proof_origin.place: H6 Lean proof: full scalar cokernel classes, geometric compatibility, flat descent, continuous integral Smith reduction and its sheaf realization are implemented. Converse, cover, stratum and coefficient transports are proved without new sorry.

Its statement permits arbitrary target types and descends scalar module isomorphism classes; this generic topological flat-descent tool is not in the restricted-functor unit.
Generic arithmetic result giving the DVR and uniformizer needed by integral Smith elimination.

Explicit pointwise formula for pulled-back integral regular-module coefficients; used entrywise to compare scalar matrices, rather than assuming a naturality clause absent from a realization statement.

Generic exact coefficient-preserving module pullback for integral coefficients, needed for finite presentations and geometric evaluation; no restricted-functor statement supplies this underived comparison.
Generic coefficient normalization at the one-point profinite set identifies evaluated integral coefficients with A; this is a point-site tool, not a replacement of the unit route.
Generic field-amalgamation lemma supplies compatible residue-field embeddings for the comparison of two presentations over one base point; the restricted-functor unit supplies no such field theorem.

lean.statement:
theorem integralLfpConstantModelComparison
    (l : ℕ) [Fact l.Prime]
    (E : Type u) [Field E] [Algebra (ℚ_[l]) E]
    [FiniteDimensional (ℚ_[l]) E]
    (X : Scheme.{u}) [CompactSpace X] [IsLocallyNoetherian X]
    (M : Mod
      (Sheaf (Scheme.ProEt.topology X) Ab.{u + 1})
      (integralCoefficientRing l E X).X) :
    IsConstructibleModuleObject
        (integralCoefficientRing l E X).X M ↔
      IsConstantModelConstructible
        (integralCondensedRing l E) X M
